blocks.h2: Algonquin Plumbing Emergencies: Call Now If
blocks.intro: Don't wait on any of these:

tiles.h3: The River Is Up and the Pump Is Down
tiles.body: A dead sump pump during high water floods a basement fast. Check the breaker, start the backup and call.

tiles.h3: The Basement Bathroom Is Backing Up
tiles.body: Often a failed ejector pump. Stop using basement fixtures.

tiles.h3: The Original Water Heater Is Leaking
tiles.body: Close the cold water valve on top of the tank.

tiles.h3: A Pipe Over the Garage Burst
tiles.body: Close the main and keep away from wet ceilings.
Leave. Call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside.
Close the shutoff behind the toilet, then call if it keeps running.

blocks.intro: Most emergency calls from Algonquin homes trace back to the river, the weather or equipment that came with the house.

items.body: The Fox River hit a record 12.70 feet at Algonquin in April 2013. On nights like that, sump pump failures come in waves. See [sump pumps](/algonquin/sump-pumps).
Heaters that came with 1990s and 2000s homes are failing now. A tank that lets go can flood a finished basement. See [water heater repair](/algonquin/water-heater-repair).
Pipes over attached garages and in exterior walls freeze first in a cold snap. See [burst pipe repair](/algonquin/burst-pipe-repair).
When an ejector pump fails, the basement bathroom backs up. See [ejector pumps](/algonquin/ejector-pump).

blocks.h2: Emergency Plumbing Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: How soon can you get to my home in Algonquin?
items.preview: Call any time. We'll give you a realistic window.
items.answer: Call us any time. Our Esplanade Drive office keeps us close to Algonquin and Lake in the Hills. Arrival times depend on the day and call volume, but we'll give you a realistic window and get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.q: My basement bathroom is backing up. Is it the sewer or the pump?
items.preview: If upstairs drains are fine, it's likely the ejector pump.
items.answer: If upstairs fixtures drain normally and only the basement is backing up, the ejector pump is the likely cause. Stop using basement fixtures and call us.

items.q: My sump pump stopped during a storm. What do I do?
items.preview: Check power, start the backup and call.
items.answer: Check that it's plugged in and the breaker hasn't tripped. If you have a backup, make sure it's running. Move valuables up off the floor and call us.

items.q: Will I know the price before you start?
items.answer: Yes. Whatever the hour, you get a flat-rate price before any work begins.

items.q: What does an emergency plumber cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on the problem. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on what's wrong and what it takes to fix it. We quote a flat rate before we start.
